# Initial values
A <- 800
B <- 200

# Parameter values
k_ba <- 0.05
k_ab <- 0.08

# Integration settings
dt <- 1
t_end <- 50
times <- seq(0, t_end, by = dt)

# Store results
A_out <- numeric(length(times))
B_out <- numeric(length(times))

# Store initial values
A_out[1] <- A
B_out[1] <- B

# Euler integration
for (i in 2:length(times)) {
  # Calculate tendencies
  dA <- k_ba * B - k_ab * A
  dB <- k_ab * A - k_ba * B

  # Update state variables
  A <- A + dA * dt
  B <- B + dB * dt

  # Store results
  A_out[i] <- A
  B_out[i] <- B
}

  E_in <- (1 - albedo) * Q
  E_out <- A + B * (T - 273.15)
  dT <- (E_in - E_out) / H
  return(dT)

heading: 6.1.2 NPZD function
text: Next, let’s define NPZD function single ocean box, neglecting transport coupling carbon cycle. simplified setup allows us focus developing intuitive understanding NPZD works.
code:
run_npzd <- function(state, params, times) {
  # Parameter values
  a <- params$a
  b <- params$b
  c <- params$c
  d <- params$d
  e <- params$e
  k <- params$k
  r_P <- params$r_P
  r_Z <- params$r_Z
  w_D <- params$w_D
  s <- params$s
  alpha <- params$alpha
  beta <- params$beta
  gamma <- params$gamma
  lambda <- params$lambda
  mu <- params$mu
  phi <- params$phi
  psi <- params$psi
  T_ref_npzd <- params$T_ref_npzd
  R_gas <- params$R_gas
  Ea_a <- params$Ea_a
  Ea_lambda <- params$Ea_lambda
  Ea_r <- params$Ea_r
  Ea_s <- params$Ea_s
  Ea_d <- params$Ea_d
  Ea_phi <- params$Ea_phi

  # Initial values
  DIN_ocn_SH <- state[["DIN_ocn_SH"]]
  P_bio_SH <- state[["P_bio_SH"]]
  Z_bio_SH <- state[["Z_bio_SH"]]
  DET_ocn_SH <- state[["DET_ocn_SH"]]
  T_ocn_SH <- state[["T_ocn_SH"]]
  A_sic <- state[["A_sic"]]

  # Store results
  N <- numeric(length(times))
  P <- numeric(length(times))
  Z <- numeric(length(times))
  D <- numeric(length(times))

  # Store initial values
  N[1] <- DIN_ocn_SH
  P[1] <- P_bio_SH
  Z[1] <- Z_bio_SH
  D[1] <- DET_ocn_SH

  # Euler integration
  dt <- times[2] - times[1]

  for (i in 2:length(times)) {
    # -------------------------
    # Arrhenius
    # -------------------------

    arrhenius <- function(r0, Ea, T_ocn, T_ref_npzd, R_gas) {
      rate <- r0 * exp(Ea / R_gas * (1 / T_ref_npzd - 1 / T_ocn))
      return(rate)
    }

    bio_rates <- function(T_ocn, A_sic) {
      a_eff <- a * (1 - A_sic)

      list(
        a_T = arrhenius(a_eff, Ea_a, T_ocn, T_ref_npzd, R_gas),
        phi_T = arrhenius(phi, Ea_phi, T_ocn, T_ref_npzd, R_gas)
      )
    }

    rates_SH <- bio_rates(T_ocn_SH, A_sic)

    # -------------------------
    # Fluxes
    # -------------------------

    # Uptake of N by P
    N_DIN2P_uptake_SH <- DIN_ocn_SH / (e + DIN_ocn_SH) * rates_SH$a_T / (b + c * P_bio_SH) * P_bio_SH

    # Grazing of P by Z
    N_P2Z_grazing_SH <- lambda * P_bio_SH^2 / (mu^2 + P_bio_SH^2) * Z_bio_SH

    # Grazing detritus
    N_P2DET_grazing_SH <- (1 - alpha - beta) * N_P2Z_grazing_SH

    # Z-growth
    N_Z_growth_SH <- alpha * N_P2Z_grazing_SH

    # Z-excretion
    N_Z2DIN_excretion_SH <- beta * N_P2Z_grazing_SH

    # Mortality of P (sinking)
    N_P2DET_mort_SH <- s * P_bio_SH

    # Mortality of Z
    N_Z2DET_mort_SH <- d * Z_bio_SH^2

    # Remineralization
    N_DET2DIN_remin_SH <- rates_SH$phi_T * DET_ocn_SH

    # -------------------------
    # Tendencies
    # -------------------------

    # Nutrients
    dDIN_bio_SH <- N_Z2DIN_excretion_SH + N_DET2DIN_remin_SH - N_DIN2P_uptake_SH

    # Phytoplankton
    dP_bio_SH <- N_DIN2P_uptake_SH - N_P2Z_grazing_SH - N_P2DET_mort_SH

    # Zooplankton
    dZ_bio_SH <- N_Z_growth_SH - N_Z2DET_mort_SH # - N_Z2DIN_RH_SH

    # Detritus
    dDET_bio_SH <- N_P2DET_mort_SH + N_Z2DET_mort_SH + N_P2DET_grazing_SH - N_DET2DIN_remin_SH

    # Rename
    dDIN_ocn_SH <- dDIN_bio_SH # assuming no transport
    dDET_ocn_SH <- dDET_bio_SH # assuming no transport

    DIN_ocn_SH <- DIN_ocn_SH + dDIN_ocn_SH * dt
    P_bio_SH <- P_bio_SH + dP_bio_SH * dt
    Z_bio_SH <- Z_bio_SH + dZ_bio_SH * dt
    DET_ocn_SH <- DET_ocn_SH + dDET_ocn_SH * dt

    # Store results
    N[i] <- DIN_ocn_SH
    P[i] <- P_bio_SH
    Z[i] <- Z_bio_SH
    D[i] <- DET_ocn_SH
  }

  df <- data.frame(N, P, Z, D)

  # Plot results
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
  days <- times / 86400
  plot(x = days, y = N, type = "l", xlab = "Days", ylab = "N (mol N / m3)", main = "(a) DIN")
  grid()
  plot(x = days, y = P, type = "l", xlab = "Days", ylab = "P (mol N / m3)", main = "(b) Phytoplankton")
  grid()
  plot(x = days, y = Z, type = "l", xlab = "Days", ylab = "Z (mol N / m3)", main = "(c) Zooplankton")
  grid()
  plot(x = days, y = D, type = "l", xlab = "Days", ylab = "D (mol N / m3)", main = "(d) Detritus")
  grid()

  return(df)
}

fun_land <- function(state, params){
# Parameter values
  NPP_0 <- params$NPP_0
  f_lnd_L <- params$f_lnd_L
  f_lnd_H <- params$f_lnd_H
  phi_lnd <- params$phi_lnd
  T_opt <- params$T_opt
  sigma_T <- params$sigma_T
  R_0 <- params$R_0
  gamma_R <- params$gamma_R
  C_ref <- params$C_ref
  T_rh <- params$T_rh

  # Initial values

  T_atm_H <- state[["T_atm_H"]]
  C_atm <- state[["C_atm"]]
  C_lnd_L <- state[["C_lnd_L"]]
  C_lnd_H <- state[["C_lnd_H"]]
  
  # Convert atmospheric C to ppmv
  C_atm_ppmv <- C_atm / 2.124
  
  T_atm_L <- seq(273 - 5, 273 + 30, 1)
  
  # Net Primary Productivity (NPP)
  NPP_lnd_L <- f_lnd_L * NPP_0 *
    (1 + phi_lnd * log(C_atm_ppmv / C_ref)) *
    exp(-(T_atm_L - T_opt)^2 / (2 * sigma_T^2))
  
  # Heterotrophic respiration
  RH_L <- C_lnd_L * R_0 * exp(gamma_R * (T_atm_L - T_rh))

13.6 Determinant
text:
matrix transforms shape spanned vectors. determinant tells us shape’s area changes, example, whether expands, shrinks, collapses line. Consider matrix:\[
\mathbf{} =
\begin{bmatrix}
& b \\
c & d \\
\end{bmatrix}
\]determinant matrix \(\mathbf{}\) defined :\[
\det(\mathbf{}) = ad -bc
\]
example:\[
\mathbf{} =
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 2 \\
1 & 0 \\
\end{bmatrix}
\]\[
\det(\mathbf{}) = 1*0 - 2*1 = -2
\]\(|\det({\mathbf{}})|>1\): area expands\(|\det({\mathbf{}})|<1\): area shrinks\(|\det({\mathbf{}})|=0\): area collapsesIn case, determinant tells us applying matrix \(\mathbf{}\) expand area spanned vectors (\(|-2|>1\)). determinant allows us calculate eigenvalues \(\lambda\):\[
\mathbf{} \mathbf{v} = \lambda \mathbf{v}
\]Let’s rewrite equation: \(\mathbf{} \mathbf{v} - \lambda \mathbf{v} = 0\)Rearrange: \((\mathbf{} - \lambda \mathbf{}) \mathbf{v} = 0\)\(\mathbf{}\) identity matrix:\[
\mathbf{} =
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 0 \\
0 & 1 \\
\end{bmatrix}
\]
\(\mathbf{v} \ne 0\), :\[
\det(\mathbf{} - \lambda \mathbf{}) = 0
\]
determinant can therefore used calculate eigenvalues. instance:\[
\mathbf{} - \lambda \mathbf{} = \begin{bmatrix} 2-\lambda & 3 \\ 1 & 4-\lambda \end{bmatrix}
\]\[
\det(\mathbf{} - \lambda \mathbf{}) = (2-\lambda)(4-\lambda) - 3 \times 1
\]\[
= (2-\lambda)(4-\lambda) - 3
\]\[
= 2 \times 4 - 2\lambda - 4\lambda + \lambda^2 - 3 = 8 - 6\lambda + \lambda^2 - 3
\]\[
= \lambda^2 - 6\lambda + 5
\]\[
\lambda^2 - 6\lambda + 5 = 0
\]\[
\lambda = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 20}}{2} = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{16}}{2} = \frac{6 \pm 4}{2}
\]\[
\Rightarrow \quad \lambda_1 = 5, \quad \lambda_2 = 1
\]

heading: 13.7 Jacobian Matrix
text:
dynamical systems theory, matrix using Jacobian matrix \(\mathbf{J}\). Jacobian matrix matrix partial derivatives describes multivariable function changes locally. instance:\[
\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}) =
\begin{bmatrix}
f_1(x, y, z) \\
f_2(x, y, z) \\
f_3(x, y, z)
\end{bmatrix}
\mathbf{J} =
\begin{bmatrix}
\frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial z} \\
\frac{\partial f_2}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial z} \\
\frac{\partial f_3}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial f_3}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial f_3}{\partial z}
\end{bmatrix}
\]eigenvalue problem becomes:\[
\det(\mathbf{J} - \lambda \mathbf{}) = 0
\]
eigenvalues \(\lambda_i\) Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}\) determine local stability type equilibrium point. eigenvalues negative real parts, equilibrium locally asymptotically stable (perturbations decay). eigenvalue positive real part, equilibrium unstable (perturbations grow). eigenvalues zero real parts, system may marginally stable.
